issues.description: Condition swallows Tab, Enter, AND every other key — hides popup on arrow keys, Escape, Backspace
issues.detail: The guard fires whenever the setting is off and the key is not Tab. That includes Up/Down/PageUp/PageDown/Escape/Backspace/printable chars. Result: popup vanishes on the first arrow-key navigation attempt. The check belongs scoped to Enter/Return specifically (Key_Return, Key_Enter), not 'not Tab'. Wrong-shape patch.

issues.description: Re-dispatching the event to textedit.keyPressEvent after hide() is a layering hack
issues.detail: Forwarding the QKeyEvent back into the parent editor from inside the popup's handler is the kind of clever-not-obvious code that bites maintainers later: double-handling, focus weirdness, recursion risk if the editor re-shows the popup. The correct shape is: don't accept the event, let Qt's normal event propagation deliver it. Call event.ignore() or return without consuming.

issues.description: get_conf() called on every keystroke instead of cached
issues.detail: This is in the hot path of keyPressEvent. Reading config through the plugin lookup chain for every key press to check a boolean is wasteful and adds latency to typing. Cache it on the widget and invalidate on config change. Not a blocker but bad taste in a code path that runs per keystroke.

issues.description: Style nit: 'not key == Qt.Key_Tab' should be 'key != Qt.Key_Tab'
issues.detail: Reads backwards. Matches no surrounding convention I can see. Trivial fixup on the way in — would not refuse for this alone, but while you're rewriting the condition to be Return/Enter-specific anyway, fix it.

issues.description: Missing default for existing configs — relies on schema default but no migration note
issues.detail: New key 'use_enter_for_completions' defaults True in the schema, which preserves behavior. Fine. But the commit message says nothing about why, and there's no test exercising the False branch. For a behavior-changing user-facing toggle in completion handling, at least one test would be cheap insurance.

review.summary: Small patch, right idea, wrong shape. The schema change and confpage addition are fine — boring, obvious, matches surrounding code. The actual logic change in completion.py is broken: 'not key == Qt.Key_Tab' means every key that isn't Tab — including arrow keys, Escape, Backspace — will hide the popup and forward the event. Users who turn this off will find their completion popup unusable. Also, re-dispatching the event to textedit.keyPressEvent from inside the popup is clever where it should be obvious — use event.ignore() and let Qt propagate. NEEDS-WORK: scope the condition to Return/Enter, drop the manual re-dispatch, cache the config read, add one test for the False path. Then it lands.
